video.title: No Money? Start This AI Website Side Hustle

summary: Chris Koerner demonstrates an AI-assisted website service for local handymen: build a tailored site quickly, show it to the owner, then charge a setup fee or monthly hosting fee. He recommends finding businesses through Google Maps and contacting them personally, and discusses free websites as an alternative way to earn trust before selling other services. He pitches GoHighLevel add-ons such as voice reception, ads, content, booking, lead generation, customer service, and email marketing. The video does not report a customer response or sale from the filmed outreach, and it includes an affiliate promotion for GoHighLevel.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; demonstrates the website workflow and pitches GoHighLevel.

speakers.name: Tyler
speakers.description: Named as the website operator whose approach prompted the demonstration; he does not speak directly in this transcript.

ideas.name: AI-built websites for local handymen
ideas.one_liner: Generate a tailored local-business website with GoHighLevel AI, show it to the owner, and charge for setup, hosting, or a monthly plan.
ideas.business_model: Website setup fee plus recurring hosting and optional upsells.
ideas.customer: Solo handyman businesses, especially those with no website or a poor one.
ideas.problem: Some handymen lack a website or have a weak one, while the host says they may value having one and have budget for it.
ideas.offer: A prebuilt, locally tailored website with service-area pages, SEO elements, a booking calendar, and CRM integration; the host suggests showing a preview before selling.

pricing.model: One-off setup plus monthly hosting, or monthly plan without setup fee; optional premium plan is mentioned but not priced.

price_points.label: Recurring website charge described for the operator's customers
Example plan with no monthly edits or custom domain
Monthly charge in the example setup-fee plan
Plan with no setup fee, custom domain, and hosting

pricing.notes: The host suggests using an entry plan to make the monthly option more attractive and says hosting has no marginal cost per added client under his account setup.

acquisition_channels.details: Search Google Maps for handymen, check their reviews, websites, service areas, and displayed phone numbers, then select small operators as prospects.

quote.text: So, we're just going to go Google Maps, Dallas, Texas Handyman.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: The host texts prospects individually from his personal iPhone, identifies himself as a nearby real person, and offers to show a site he says he just built. This is unsolicited marketing by text; in the UK, PECR generally requires consent to send marketing texts to individuals and sole traders.

quote.text: I'm going to use my actual iPhone to text local business owners here in the Dallas Fort Worth area and say, "Hey, I built you a free website."
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: The host suggests visiting listed business addresses, knocking on doors, and showing the site on a laptop or iPad. He says some addresses may be the owner's home.

quote.text: I'm going to go do this in person. I'm going to go to a retail store. I'm going to go to the addresses listed on these businesses.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Use GoHighLevel AI to generate the site, then review or copy the HTML into its AI Studio if needed. The host says to tailor the business name, location, service areas, and phone number, connect the site to the account calendar, and show it to the owner. Human prospect research, personalization, and sales are still part of the demonstrated process.
unit_economics_claims: The host describes the operator's maintenance cost as almost zero and says marginal monthly costs do not rise as clients are added.
The host claims 100 customers at $75 per month would produce $7,500 per month, or almost $100,000 per year, before substantial marginal costs.
The host says the website subscription can cover overhead and that upsells are where more revenue could come from.
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated; the host describes the operator's upfront cost as almost zero and mentions a GoHighLevel trial, but does not establish the full account cost or required plan.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated. The host says the site can be generated in minutes, but the filmed outreach produces no reported response or sale.

acquisition.how: The demonstrated channels are manual prospect selection, unsolicited texts, and possible door knocking. UK marketing texts to sole traders require consent, and in-person sales require a human.

onboarding.how: AI can generate a draft and CRM workflows can help, but a person must verify the business details, obtain customer approval, and configure the account.

delivery.how: An agent can generate and adapt much of a template site; a person should check the content, local claims, links, booking flow, and mobile display.

billing.how: Recurring subscription billing can be handled by software after plan setup, with occasional human review for failed payments and changes.

support.how: Routine hosting questions may be automated, but edits, disputes, and business-specific requests need human review.

uk_applicability.notes: The service and software workflow can work in the UK, but local SEO, domains, pricing, and customer expectations need localisation. The demonstrated unsolicited text outreach to sole traders is restricted by PECR; use consent-based or inbound acquisition, or check UK rules for other outreach.

risks: The host's proposed unsolicited text outreach to handyman owners would create UK PECR risk if aimed at individuals or sole traders without consent.
The host warns against mass texting and scraping but still demonstrates individual cold texts; this does not establish that the method is lawful in the UK.
AI-generated pages may contain inaccurate service details, locations, SEO claims, or booking information unless checked.
A prospect may reject the site, and the host reports no response or sale before ending the filmed outreach.
A free or low-priced site can create support and edit obligations that exceed the subscription revenue.
The claimed near-zero marginal cost depends on the GoHighLevel plan and account structure and is not independently verified.
